svg.title: ARCH vs GARCH
svg.desc: ARCH counts past squared shocks one by one; GARCH recycles yesterday's variance and compresses the same memory into two parameters.
svg.text: ARCH vs GARCH — the memory of volatility
Squared past shocks alone vs squared shocks plus yesterday's variance
Finite — cuts off at lag q
read from the sum of α
back to the unconditional variance in a few periods
finite weights that cut off at lag q
Weights α1 … α4, zero after that
More memory means proportionally more parameters
the long exponential tail β creates
Two parameters express an infinite memory
A shock dies out in a period or two
Returns to unconditional volatility almost at once
The aftermath of a shock lingers
The closer α+β is to 1, the slower the return
ARCH counts past squared shocks directly; GARCH recycles yesterday's variance.
Persistence is read from α+β, and neither model distinguishes good news from bad.
A single β replaces infinitely many
Next: capturing asymmetry — EGARCH and GJR.
